svg.text: 21 agents across 5 departments generate a company; an operating layer then runs it on cadences under human supervision
GENERATION LAYER · runs once, produces the opening state
LangGraph · 21 agents · 5 departments · staged nested graphs
stage 1 → stage 2 concurrent → stage 3 join barrier
an agent may write only its own department section; a cross-department write is rejected
Finding that drives the layer above: prompt-level numeric bounds were ignored repeatedly, so cross-agent constraints are enforced in code.
OPERATING LAYER · runs indefinitely, operates that state
the plan becomes the company's opening state, not the deliverable
spend caps · no data deletion · no payment without verification
approves, rejects, arbitrates — an approval never unlocks a hard constraint
• audit trail and ledger are append-only, enforced by database triggers
• 5 isolated department memory stores, 4 typed each
• retrieved data overrides generated data for the same field
• every record keeps a source label
• ordered fallback chain; a run completes even when hosted tiers are exhausted
• no agent imports a vendor SDK
Anchors are computed, never reported: no department, planner, worker or reflection process can write one — there is no anchor table, so there is nowhere to write.
